articles.title: Why Elon Musk is taking on India's richest man over Starlink
articles.summary: Musk has taken pot-shots at Reliance owner Mukesh Ambani as Starlink struggles to launch in India.

blocks.text: Elon Musk has questioned whether billionaire Mukesh Ambani is the "real boss of India" as his satellite internet company Starlink struggles to secure final approval to launch in the country.

The remark came a day after Musk accused unnamed powerful business interests of trying to block Starlink's entry into India. He then singled out Ambani, whose Reliance conglomerate owns Jio, India's biggest mobile network operator.
India has rejected Musk's allegations, saying its satellite communications rules are fair and non-discriminatory.
Ambani and Reliance Group have not responded to Musk's remarks. The BBC has reached out to them for comment
The row comes as competition grows in India's satellite internet market, with Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel also preparing to launch services.
The rivalry is complicated by the fact that Starlink has also partnered with Ambani's Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel.

In March 2025, both companies signed agreements with SpaceX to distribute Starlink equipment and services in India, subject to government approval. The companies also said they could explore sharing network infrastructure. The BBC has also reached out to Bharti Airtel for comment.
Musk first made the allegations on Wednesday, accusing "certain oligarchs" of maintaining a "monopolistic chokehold" on Indian consumers.
"You can guess who they are," he wrote on X, external, adding that blocking Starlink was "a crime against the people of India".

On Thursday, India's Ministry of Communications responded, saying that three operators - Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Jio Satellite Communications - were at broadly the same stage of the approval process, with all three awaiting security clearances and spectrum allocation before they can launch commercial services.
"The suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived," the ministry said, without naming Musk directly.
Musk continued to question the delay, saying Starlink was already licensed in more than 165 countries.

"Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license? Is Ambani the real boss of India?" he wrote on X on Thursday.

Starlink, owned by Musk's SpaceX, uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide internet access, particularly in remote areas where mobile networks and broadband cables are difficult or expensive to install.
The company has been trying to enter India since 2021 and has secured key licences. But it still needs final security clearances and spectrum allocation before it can begin commercial services.

Wednesday's row unfolded as senior executives from Starlink, Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel gathered at the India Mobile Congress in Delhi, where all three companies discussed their plans for satellite internet services.

Speaking at the event, Akash Ambani, chairman of Reliance Jio Infocomm and Mukesh Ambani's son, said the company was developing its own satellite communications technology and working towards regulatory approvals.
Asked by a reporter about Musk's allegations, Akash declined to comment and only said, "We want to be heads down and deliver value to our Indian consumers."
Bharti Airtel chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said his company's satellite venture was also awaiting government approvals.

SpaceX executive Lauren Dreyer, who oversees Starlink's business operations, said the company had spent years working with Indian regulators and had built security controls into its network to meet the country's requirements.

Security has been a key concern surrounding Starlink's entry into India. In 2024, Indian authorities said they had recovered Starlink equipment during a drug-smuggling investigation in the remote Andaman and Nicobar Islands and an army operation in the northeastern state of Manipur.
Musk said at that time that Starlink's service had never been active in India, arguing that the equipment recovered by authorities could not have been using its satellite network.
Questions also remain over how affordable the service would be for Indian consumers, particularly those in rural areas.
India is one of the world's largest internet markets but access remains uneven, particularly in remote areas where mobile networks and broadband cables are difficult or expensive to build.

Musk has argued that Starlink could help bridge this gap. "Starlink in India would enable high-speed, affordable internet connectivity for those who can't afford current prices or who don't have a connection at all!" he wrote on X on Wednesday.
The company has yet to announce prices for India, but some experts say its plans elsewhere suggest the service could be beyond the reach of many Indian households.
In the US, Starlink's residential plans start at $55 a month, although prices and equipment costs vary by plan and location.

articles.title: Holborn and St Pancras byelection loss will disappoint Greens – but there may also be relief
articles.summary: It may sound odd to think Zack Polanski would be happy with second place, but after the most challenging week of his political life it could have been worse

blocks.text: Parliamentary byelections can generate all sorts of emotional responses, often very strong ones. But for the main contenders in Holborn and St Pancras, the feeling this morning might be more prosaic: relief.

For Labour, Sagal Abdi-Wali’s victory with just over 45% of the total vote was widely expected, but it allows the party to credibly claim Andy Burnham as a politician able to reach people in both Reform-leaning areas such as Makerfield, and in Green-friendly inner cities.

Retaining a constituency formerly held by your last leader, Keir Starmer, and which has been overwhelmingly Labour since it was created in 1983, is in normal political times not that notable an achievement, but these are not normal times.

A low turnout of 38.7% and Abdi-Wali’s numerically modest 3,364 majority that resulted might not appear the greatest endorsement of the government, but it is also likely to have been in part due to the widespread assumption that Labour would win.

And what of the Greens, and particularly Zack Polanski, the party’s leader in England and Wales, who decided to go for the high-profile seat himself? Again, it may sound curious to think he would be happy with second place, but after the most challenging week of his political life it could have been worse.

Polanski got just under 33% of the vote, well above anyone else apart from Abdi-Wali, a proportion which shows that in an another election, and up against a Labour party not enjoying a Burnham bounce, the Greens could still be highly competitive in seats like these.

When Polanski said he wanted to stand, the hope was for another wave of enthusiasm and publicity of the sort that propelled Hannah Spencer to victory in February in another supposedly safe Labour seat, Gorton and Denton.

He will nonetheless be quietly pleased that the result does not seem to have shown much of a shedding of Green votes after criticisms of, and deep divisions in, the party since it adopted a highly controversial policy on Zionism and Israel last weekend.

The new policy, decided by members at the Greens’ annual conference, equates Zionism, the movement for a Jewish state, with racism, and calls for Israel to be replaced by a single Palestinian state. It is publicly opposed by four of the party’s five MPs, with numerous councillors distancing themselves as well and a handful resigning.

Polanski’s decision to not take a side, and even to absent himself from Sunday’s debate so he could campaign in the byelection, has prompted deep unease among some Greens, who termed it a failure of leadership.
It was notable that after the result, Polanski had to insist that he intended to stay as Green leader. “Yes absolutely, that’s what leaders do,” he replied.

While some in the Greens had questioned Polanski’s decision to contest a seat in north London, rather than east London, where he lives, his allies make the point that Nigel Farage took eight tries to become an MP.

Either way, the result has not made Polanski’s position any worse. Had the Green vote collapsed he would have been under very intense pressure. As it stands, he must try to reassure sceptics in the party before seeking re-election in a year from now, under the party’s policy of two-year terms for leaders.
And what of the others? The Conservatives will be quietly happy with beating Reform UK to take third place, their 7.1% being almost exactly the same proportion of votes as they took in 2024.

This might not seem like much of an achievement, but the party’s national poll ratings remain stubbornly below 2024 levels, and thus stasis will most likely be claimed as more evidence of a Badenoch bounce.

Way down in fifth place, the emotions begin the switch. While they are byelection specialists, the Liberal Democrats were never going to win here, but they had put in at least some effort to boost their vote, with MPs going out this week to knock on doors.

Coming behind Reform on just over 3% of the vote will be a disappointment. Amid the noisy debates over the leadership of Labour, the Tories and Greens, it can be easy to overlook the disquiet among some of Ed Davey’s MPs that the Lib Dems do not appear to be cutting through. He will not be feeling relief this morning.

articles.title: Malaysia shuts schools amid toxic haze from Indonesian fires
articles.summary: Toxic smoke from forest fires in Indonesia has pushed air pollution to unhealthy levels, prompting authorities in Malaysia to take emergency measures.

image.caption: Kuala Lumpur's skyline has been shrouded in haze for weeksImage: Wong Fok Loy/SOPA Images/IMAGO

blocks.text: Malaysian authorities closed schools in the capital, Kuala Lumpur, and other parts of the country on Friday due to haze caused by forest fires in nearby Indonesia.

"I have instructed all state education departments and district education offices to continue monitoring the haze situation and take immediate action if conditions require it," Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said in a statement.
The minister announced which schools would be fully closed and which would continue operating partially in five states and two federal territories.
"Going forward, we will ensure that any decision to close schools is communicated in advance so that parents have enough time to prepare," Fadhlina added.

blocks.caption: Indonesia has been struggling to contain a series of forest fires Image: Elly Priatno/DW

blocks.text: Deteriorating air quality
Air quality measurements in Kuala Lumpur remain at "unhealthy" levels, with Swiss air-quality monitor IQAir ranking the Malaysian capital among the most polluted cities in the world.
Malaysia's King Sultan Ibrahim weighed in on the issue on Thursday, saying schools should be closed whenever air-quality readings reach 150 or higher on the Air Pollutant Index (API).
API readings above 200 are considered very unhealthy, while levels above 300 are deemed hazardous. Readings exceeding 500 constitute the threshold for declaring a local emergency.
Kuala Lumpur recorded an API reading of 170 on Friday.

The city lies about 1,200 kilometers (745 miles) from Indonesia, where a wave of forest fires has affected millions of people since August. According to IQAir, Kuala Lumpur is currently the world's second most polluted city, behind only neighboring Singapore.
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday that Indonesian President Prabowo ​Subianto had ⁠agreed to take measures to tackle the haze, but did not provide more details.

articles.title: Marcos says he'll attend Singapore F1 race: Happy coincidence
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Friday described his attendance at the Formula 1 race over the weekend as “a happy coincidence.”

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 2:32pm
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Friday described his attendance at the Formula 1 race over the weekend as “a happy coincidence.”
Marcos is in Singapore on a working visit.

Asked if he will be at the car race, Marcos said, “Yes, happy coincidence. All of these, the Forbes CEO, all of these meetings that I’m having happened… because what's happened with the Singapore F1, it's become such an event that all these other events are scheduled around it because so many people come.”
“I once came before I was president a long time ago, and I came to watch just to watch the race… And I was walking around, I met Lee Kuan Yew,” Marcos said.

“And I came to the conclusion: you come to the Singapore F1, you can meet anybody, everyone that you want. Even some of the businessmen from the Philippines, I had meetings with them because they were there for the F1.,” he added.

Asked about the benefits of his watching the race for the country, Marcos said, “It’s sometimes it's just a question of starting a discussion that you cannot start in any other way. You pick up the phone, and you say, you know, let's talk about this.”

“It's not the same as when you sit down over coffee, and you say, okay, okay, we'll continue this. So in the future, when you talk about it, the person you're talking to knows already what you're talking about, has an idea of what,” Marcos said.

“And we all know, especially for Asians, the face-to-face meeting is the most important part of any relationship, be it a be it a familial relationship, a business relationship, a political relation, any kind of relationship,” he added. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Halle Berry is denying child abuse claims by her ex-husband. Here's what we know
articles.summary: Halle Berry is denying allegations made by her ex-husband Olivier Martinez, who has filed for sole custody and a restraining order, accusing her of physically abusing their 13-year-old son, Maceo.…

image.caption: Halle Berry attends the world premiere of Amazon MGM Studios' Crime 101 at the United Theater on Broadway in Los Angeles in February 2026. (Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Halle Berry is denying allegations made by her ex-husband Olivier Martinez, who has filed for sole custody and a restraining order, accusing her of physically abusing their 13-year-old son, Maceo. Her 18-year-old daughter has come to her defence.
A temporary restraining order is in place ahead of an Oct. 16 hearing

Halle Berry is denying allegations by her ex-husband Olivier Martinez that she physically abused their 13-year-old son, Maceo, as the former couple heads toward an Oct. 16 court hearing over custody and a restraining order.

Martinez has asked for sole legal and physical custody of Maceo and a restraining order against Berry, alleging she was violent toward their son during a Sept. 26 incident and claiming a history of abuse, according to court documents obtained by CBC News.

A Los Angeles Superior Court judge granted a temporary restraining order on Oct. 1, restricting Berry's parenting time and ordering her to stay 100 yards from Martinez until the hearing. The judge denied Martinez's request that Berry's sobriety be monitored, citing insufficient information.

Berry has denied the allegations, calling them "absolutely false" and stating that she has "never physically, emotionally or otherwise abused Maceo." She described the Sept. 26 incident as playful roughhousing that escalated into an argument and is asking the court to restore their 50-50 custody arrangement.
Berry and Martinez married in 2013, welcomed Maceo later that year and finalized their divorce in 2023 with a joint custody arrangement.
Actors Olivier Martinez, left, and Halle Berry attend the premiere of the CBS science-fiction drama Extant at the California Science Center in Los Angeles in June 2014. (Mark Davis/Getty Images)
Here's how the legal battle has unfolded
Oct. 1: Martinez seeks restraining order, sole custody

Martinez files a request for a temporary restraining order covering both himself and Maceo, writing that he needed protection because Berry "physically abused our son by jumping on him and choking him" on Sept. 26.
He also asked the court to modify their 50-50 custody arrangement and require Berry to undergo sobriety monitoring.
In his declaration, viewed by CBC News, Martinez says he received a frantic call from Maceo asking to be picked up and could hear Berry yelling in the background.

He alleges the confrontation began while Maceo was playing a game in his bedroom and that Berry pushed him before grabbing him around the neck and choking him. Martinez also alleges "there have been other instances of abuse over the course of the last few years."
His filing references text messages between him and Berry, including one in which she says: "I feel terrible about what happened last night as I know he does as well."
Oct. 3: Nahla defends her mother
Nahla, Berry's 18-year-old daughter with ex-partner Gabriel Aubry, filed a declaration defending her mother.
"I have never seen my mom hit, slap, choke, grab, or physically abuse Maceo in any way," Nahla wrote in a declaration.
Halle Berry speaks during SiriusXM's Front Row Series with the cast of Crime 101 at SiriusXM Studios in New York City in February 2026. (Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images for SiriusXM)
Berry pushes back
Oct. 4: Berry challenges allegations
Berry's lawyer submitted court documents disputing Martinez's allegations and pointing to what Berry described as previous violations of court orders and legal sanctions involving their son's needs.
Berry's legal team also says video evidence contradicts Martinez's account.
Oct. 5: Berry gives her account
Berry filed a declaration directly denying Martinez's allegations and describing what she says happened on Sept. 26.

"I have never physically, emotionally, or otherwise abused Maceo," Berry wrote. "I am a victim of domestic violence, and I help victims of domestic violence." She added: "I am not a perpetrator of violence. I would never hurt our child."
She said she went into Maceo's room to tell him it was time to stop playing a game and began recording him when he continued.
Berry said that when Maceo noticed her filming, he grabbed her phone and they began "playfully roughhousing," something she says they "frequently do."
She denied putting her hands around Maceo's neck, choking him or restricting his breathing.

Berry said Maceo then "unexpectedly" became upset "after the playfulness ended" and pushed her. Then she tried to take his gaming headset off. She said her fiancé, Van Hunt, got between them before Maceo said he would call his father and leave the house.
Berry said that while Maceo "may not always like the rules I set," he requires "structure and continuous contact with his mother rather than a separation resulting from cruel, manufactured claims."
Berry is asking the court to restore the previous 50-50 custody arrangement.
The next hearing is scheduled for Oct. 16, when the court is expected to consider whether the temporary restrictions should remain in place or be changed.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Griffin Jaeger is a reporter and producer with CBC's entertainment unit. He also formerly hosted and produced content for The National’s digital platforms. You can reach him at griffin.jaeger@cbc.ca

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 2:19pm
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. is not affected by the latest drop in his satisfaction rating, Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said Friday.

“Kahit bumaba, hindi naaapektuhan ang Pangulo. Tuloy-tuloy ang pagtatrabaho–hindi nagbabakasyon, nagtatrabaho… So again, ang numero ng survey firms hindi po ‘yan makakaapekto sa pagtatrabaho ng Pangulo,” Castro said during a press briefing in Singapore.
(Even with this decline, the President remains unaffected. He continues to work non-stop without taking a break… So again, numbers from any survey firms will not hinder the President's work.)
“Very timely lang kasi ang paglabas nito dahil maraming issue na kinasasangkutan ngayon ang Bise Presidente,”
(The timing of its release is quite notable, coming right as the Vice President faces numerous issues.)
The President's satisfaction rating fell to -11 points, according to a recent survey conducted by the Social Weather Stations (SWS) and released Thursday.
The survey showed that as of September 2026, 35% of adult Filipinos were satisfied with Marcos’ performance, 20% were undecided, and 46% were dissatisfied.
This produced a net satisfaction score of -11, categorized as “poor” by the polling firm. This is a four-point drop from his -7 “neutral” rating in June.
Nonetheless, this latest score remains higher than Marcos’ record-low rating of -15 recorded in March 2026. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Adidas accuses Australian label White Fox of ‘trading off its reputation’ with use of four-stripe branding
articles.summary:
Global sportswear brand is suing online retailer in the federal court for selling clothes featuring ‘deceptively similar’ design

  • Get our

blocks.text: Global sportswear brand Adidas claims Australian label White Fox is trying to trade off its reputation by infringing its distinctive three-stripe trademark.
Adidas is suing the online fast-fashion retailer in the Federal Court for selling clothes with a four-stripe design, which it argues is deceptively similar to its classic design.
White Fox rejected repeated requests to stop selling and promoting clothing bearing the four parallel stripes, its rival claims.
During the first mention of the dispute on Friday, Adidas’s barrister Patrick Flynn SC argued the Sydney-based company had been using the stripes as a trademark for months.
He pointed to a picture of a White Fox-endorsed influencer wearing the company’s four-stripe shorts with genuine Adidas shoes as a promotion that would confuse consumers.
“There’s an intention to trade off our reputation,” Flynn said.
Adidas has held the trademark for a three-stripe design in Australia for more than 50 years and successfully sued another retailer for infringement over shoes bearing four stripes in 2013.
It meant the action filed against White Fox in September was “not uncharted territory”, Flynn noted.
“This is a pretty simple matter,” he said.
White Fox’s barrister Ed Heerey KC said the Australian company would argue the four stripes emblazoned on the label’s clothing were simply decorative rather than a trademark.

blocks.caption: (L-R) Adidas track pants alongside White Fox track pants. Composite: Federal Court of Australia

blocks.text: He highlighted similar items bearing the four stripes from other brands such as fast-fashion labels Princess Polly, Glassons, and Shein.
“Obviously Adidas has a reputation,” Heerey said.
“Their own slogan is that it’s the brand with three stripes. Emphasis on the three.”
The boutique will interrogate whether the use of four stripes was deceptively similar to Adidas’s trademark and whether any consumers would actually be misled.
after newsletter promotion
He noted the 2013 judgment in favour of Adidas found it was common for branding to be placed on the side of shoes, but there was no such common practice for clothing.
Adidas is seeking orders that will prevent White Fox making clothing with four stripes and force it to hand over profits it made on the products.
Justice Ian Jackman – brother of one of Australia’s most famous exports Hugh Jackman – set the dispute down for a hearing in early 2027.
It marks the first high-profile litigation of this kind against White Fox Boutique, which has become a major player in the retail industry since it was launched in Sydney in 2013.
Co-founders Georgia and Daniel Contos, who own the company with Daniel’s mother Melina Maceri, focused on social media and influencer marketing to build their brand.
The online retailer later expanded to the US and UK and generated $542m in revenue in the year to June 2025.
Meanwhile Adidas, which generated a record $39.9bn in 2025, has vigilantly defended its three-stripe trademark across the globe with varying success.
The sportswear giant recently lost its trademark infringement cases against luxury brand Thom Browne in the US, UK, and Germany.
The upcoming battle in the federal court could prove to be a battleground for Adidas in a world of fast fashion and prolific imitation.

articles.title: House prosecution team drops bribery article against Sara Duterte
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel has filed a manifestation with the Senate impeachment court that it will drop Article III or the bribery charges in the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 2:05pm Updated October 9, 2026 2:19pm
The House prosecution panel has filed a manifestation with the Senate impeachment court that it will drop Article III or the bribery charges in the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
In a press conference on Friday, House prosecutor Keith Flores said the prosecution had reached a decision and informed the Senate tribunal.

"I think we already filed our manifestation last Tuesday pa that we will be dropping bribery… the team already came to a decision (that) we will end with Article II," Flores said, referring to charges against Duterte relating to alleged unexplained wealth.

"It's totally at the discretion of the prosecution team po kung anong articles ang ipro-prosecute nila and in this particular case, we did all three articles except for Article III, which is bribery," he added.
(It's totally at the discretion of the prosecution team which articles they will prosecute, and in this particular case, we did all three articles except for Article III, which is bribery.)
Flores said the dropping of the article had little to do with the strength of their case, saying the prosecution was merely conscious of the timetable that they set for themselves.
This timetable Flores is referring to is not the timeline that the prosecution set during the pre-trial however.

"We think we have already presented enough on all the three articles and to drag it further pa na i-include na pa namin yung bribery, might be stretching the patience not only of the people, but also of the senator-judges," Flores said.

(We think we have already presented enough on all the three articles and to drag it further to include bribery might be stretching the patience not only of the people, but also of the senator-judges.)

The House prosecution has already presented three out of the four articles of impeachment originally filed against Duterte. The first of which was the Article IV or the alleged grave threats against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former speaker Martin Romualdez, which was followed by Article I or the misuse of confidential funds.
Article II or the unexplained wealth charge is currently being taken up in the impeachment court.
House prosecutor 1-Rider party-list Representative Rodge Gutierrez maintained that their case remained strong.
"All articles that were filed in the impeachment… would stand on their own," Gutierrez said.

Article III refers to the allegation that the Duterte must be impeached for committing bribery by giving monetary gifts or payments to Department of Education (DepEd) officials to induce the violation and circumvention of procurement and other related laws. — VDV, GMA News

The Cockroach Janta Party claims authorities are carrying out mass arrests ahead of its planned protest on October 10. Founder 'Cockroach' Abhijeet Dipke has accused the Modi government of "intimidation." DW has more.

blocks.text: Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
October 9, 2026
India's Cockroach movement claims thousands detained ahead of Jantar Mantar march

As the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) ramps up its call for a protest march in New Delhi on October 10 over alleged voter roll manipulation, the youth-led movement has accused India's authorities of mass detentions of its members.
CJP spokesperson Deepak Baliyan and activists from across the country were among those arrested, CJP leaders said in a series of social media posts on Thursday night.
Baliyan was released later in the evening after being arrested by Rajasthan police at his house, CJP Co-Convener Ashutosh Ranka said on X on Friday.
Ranka claimed that at least 10,000 people were detained country-wide on Thursday.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged on X that a group of the movement's volunteers from the state of Telangana were arrested by Madhya Pradesh police onboard a train in Bhopal.

The movement earlier said that a group of students from the western Indian city of Pune who were headed for the planned protest in Delhi were also detained. The CJP said they were being taken on a bus to an unknown location.
There have been no police statements on the alleged detentions so far.
Cockroach movement describes detentions as 'emergency'
Leaders of the CJP have railed against the alleged mass arrests, likening the situation to a "state of emergency."
"Why not just declare EMERGENCY?", Dipke said as he reacted to a video of the students from Pune purportedly being detained.

The last time an emergency decree was issued in India was under former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in the mid-70s. Emergency powers were applied by the Congress leader for 21 months, with civil liberties being suspended, most of the opposition being jailed and media censored.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) calls the period a "dark chapter" in India's history.
Another prominent CJP spokesperson Saurav Das accused the Modi government of being "at war with its own young citizens."
"Hello India. We are under a State of Emergency," Das wrote on X.
CJP's Abhijeet Dipke set to arrive in Delhi on October 10
Meanwhile, founder 'Cockroach' Dipke has said that he will land in Delhi on Saturday and march to Jantar Mantar.
"This intimidation is not going to work, Modi. The youth of this country are no longer scared of you," Dipke said.

Thousands are expected to converge at the capital's Jantar Mantar protest site on Saturday to participate in CJP's protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a controversial revision of voter lists.
Jantar Mantar served as ground-zero for the viral online Cockroach movement's debut protest in July which culminated with the resignation of the then-education minister.
The CJP, opposition parties and their student units have been holding near-daily demonstrations against Kumar.
Around 130 million names have been removed from electoral rolls under an exercise called Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
Opposition leaders and critics say that those struck off the lists include a huge number of minority voters.
They accuse Modi's BJP of using the exercise as a tool to secure future electoral gains, questioning the independence of the Election Commission of India (ECI), which is overseeing the exercise.
The ECI and the BJP deny the allegations.

articles.title: Virgin unveils its future cross-Channel train as it gears up to take on Eurostar
articles.summary:
Group plans to launch services from London in 2030 and hopes to outshine competitor with design inspiration from its airline, cruise and hotel arms

Flash interiors, fancy food and maybe even…

blocks.text: Flash interiors, fancy food and maybe even a bar: Virgin has unveiled a mock-up of its future cross-Channel train, with a pledge to create “something genuinely new”.
The group is planning to launch rail services from London to the continent in 2030, with Eurostar facing competition for the first time since the opening of the Channel tunnel.
Virgin has ordered 12 trains from the manufacturer Alstom, and will hope to outshine Eurostar on design and customer experience as it fits them out.

While Virgin’s last stab at reimagining UK train travel may have peaked with the talking toilet seat on its intercity services in 2013, it has said the future trains will be inspired from its airline, cruise and hotel arms.

Although details are being kept firmly under wraps, it said it would draw on Virgin Atlantic’s airport lounges, or Clubhouses, for “pre-departure and onboard social spaces” with “more flexibility to work, relax or socialise in style”. Food will be influenced by its cruise line menu and the design by its Virgin Hotels brand.

Josh Bayliss, the chief executive of Virgin Group, said: “Virgin has a proud history in UK rail. With our latest venture we are drawing on more than four decades of experience across travel and hospitality to create something genuinely new.

“We’re confident that more journeys between the UK and Europe will be made by train. We’re adding capacity for millions more international rail journeys each year, growing the market as a whole. We’re looking forward to seeing our distinctive red and black trains travelling across Europe.”
Virgin will also look to connect its rail and airline networks, potentially bringing passengers from France for Virgin Atlantic flights.

The Office of Rail and Road on Thursday published an agreement with Eurostar for Virgin to maintain its trains at the Temple Mills international depot in east London, with track access in the UK confirmed until at least 2040.
after newsletter promotion

Italy’s state-owned Trenitalia is also expected to launch cross-Channel high-speed services. It already runs international trains as far as Paris and recently announced its own €2bn order for 19 new trains from Hitachi, some of which are expected to be based in France and run through the tunnel to London.

articles.title: Sydney trader sacked for working from Singapore without permission wins unfair dismissal case
articles.summary:
Employee had also been in Bali when he told his manager he was working from home, Fair Work Commission hears

  • Get our
articles.byline: Nino Bucci Courts and justice reporter

blocks.text: A Sydney currency trader who was sacked for working from Singapore without approval has won an unfair dismissal case, but failed to be awarded compensation.
The Fair Work Commission ruled on Wednesday that Charles Graham had been unfairly dismissed by HIFX Australia, trading as Xe, in December last year.
Graham was sacked after his manager asked an IT worker to use his “FBI skills” and track the IP address on Graham’s laptop.

They discovered he was working from Singapore. It was also later discovered he had previously worked from Bali after telling his manager he was working from home because he had a plumber “coming around to sort out some recurring bathroom issues”.
Graham was sacked as Xe found he knew he had to get prior approval to work overseas and was to attend the office three times a week.
He said he had been holidaying in Singapore before his partner became ill with a bacterial infection, preventing him from returning to Australia.
He provided documentation, which he said showed his partner required medical treatment.
Graham had previously asked Xe if he could relocate to Singapore, but his request was denied.

Fair Work Commission commissioner Alana Matheson said that after the company sent an email to Graham advising him of its discovery on 17 November last year, the “tone … had clearly pivoted” by the following day, when he was told “there was a case to answer regarding alleged breaches of company policy”.
Over the following 10 days, a series of further email exchanges and a discussion between Xe managers took place.

Graham said in his written response to Xe that he travelled to Singapore for a holiday and that there was no relation to his previous request to relocate there, that the decision to reschedule the return flight to Australia was made over a weekend, and that as there was no expectation or precedent that he contacted his manager outside business hours, he could not inform them of this.

He said that when he did log on from Singapore rather than in Australia “he was bombarded with triaging hundreds of unread emails from his time off, fielding inbound calls and dealing with an eligible complaint from a high-value client”, and this took priority over telling his manager he was stuck overseas.

Among his other responses was that he only intended to spend a short amount of time overseas, he had not been told about specific policies regarding hybrid work, and that he had intended to let his manager know he was overseas as soon as practicable.

The company was not swayed and on 2 December last year sent him a termination letter that stated it had carefully reviewed his written submissions and found that he had not provided flight screenshots with his name, medical evidence that showed his partner was unable to travel, an adequate explanation for not telling his manager he was in Singapore, and had previously complied with “absence and approval processes”, demonstrating that he was familiar with them and had instead made “a conscious choice not to follow” them.
after newsletter promotion
“Your conduct represents a serious breach of company policy, a failure to follow lawful and reasonable instructions, and an irreparable breakdown of trust and confidence,” it said in the letter.
Graham told the commission he worked remotely twice before November 2025: the previous year from Townsville, and in April and May 2025 from Bali. He had been employed by Xe for 20 months.
But his manager said she had not been aware he had ever worked remotely from overseas.

A Microsoft Teams message from Graham to his manager was included in evidence before the commission that detailed his claim he was working from home as he had a plumbing issue during one of the days he also told the commission he worked from Bali.
Matheson found that she was satisfied that the dismissal of Graham was unreasonable because while there was a valid reason for his dismissal, the process followed was procedurally unfair.
This was because Xe failed to fully raise the matters it was relying on in making the decision to dismiss Graham, Matheson said.
She found that reinstatement was inappropriate but also decided against awarding compensation.
This was, she said, in part because his misconduct contributed to the decision to dismiss him, and he was paid four weeks in lieu of notice.

articles.title: PNP looking into reported PH-bound drugs seized in Laos, Thailand
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Friday said it is coordinating with foreign authorities to verify reports that separate shipments of illegal drugs seized in Laos and Thailand were allegedly…

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 1:45pm

The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Friday said it is coordinating with foreign authorities to verify reports that separate shipments of illegal drugs seized in Laos and Thailand were allegedly bound for the Philippines.

PNP spokesperson Police Colonel Allen Rae Co said local authorities were checking the details of the reported seizures including the origin of the shipment, their intended destinations, ownership of the aircraft, and its flight plan.
"It was the claim of the Laotian or the Malaysian authorities lang na it's bound for the Philippines," he said at a press briefing.
"So we are verifying and we are already coordinating through the proper channels with the Laotian and Malaysian authorities," he added.
On Wednesday, the South China Morning Post reported that 521 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine were seized by Laotian authorities from a private jet.
The drugs were allegedly bound for Manila.
Co said the PNP was coordinating with authorities in Laos and Malaysia to verify the reported information, including the ownership of the aircraft and its flight plan.
The PNP was also checking a separate report involving a shipment of over a ton of crystal methamphetamine allegedly in Thailand.
On Thursday, the Bangkok Post reported that police have seized more than a ton of crystal methamphetamine worth 1.2 billion baht (about P2.2 billion) from a boat in the Gulf of Thailand.
The seized items were reportedly being transported to the Philippines.
Co warned against concluding that the drugs were intended for the Philippines, saying the reports remained unconfirmed.

"We are glad na hindi na nakarating po dito sa ating itong mga droga na ito. But as to the claim na ito po talaga ay destined for the country, it's premature to conclude whether it's true or not," he said.
(We are glad that these drugs have not reached our country. But as for the claim that this is really destined for the country, it's premature to conclude whether it is true or not.)
He assured that the PNP continues to monitor international drug-smuggling activities. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Prosecution drops bribery case vs Sara Duterte
articles.summary: 'The decision to not proceed with the bribery [charge] had nothing to do with the strength of the case,' prosecutor Keith Flores says

blocks.text: House prosecutor Keith Flores listens to the testimony of a witness during Day 32 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on October 1, 2026.
Senate Social Media Unit
'The decision to not proceed with the bribery [charge] had nothing to do with the strength of the case,' prosecutor Keith Flores says
MANILA, Philippines – The prosecution will no longer present its bribery case against Vice President Sara Duterte in a bid to expedite her trial.
House prosecutor Keith Flores told the media on Friday, October 9, that the prosecution had informed the impeachment court about its decision in a filing on Tuesday, October 6.

“The decision to not proceed with the bribery (charge) had nothing to do with the strength of the case. We’re conscious about the timetable that the prosecution set for us to prosecute the entire articles of impeachment. But it no longer fit the timetable that we set to ourselves,” said Flores, who leads the team on the bribery case.
This means that the prosecution will end its presentation of evidence with its case on her alleged unexplained wealth. The prosecution had been mulling over the possibility since early September.

During the House good government committee inquiry in 2024, then-DepEd special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda claimed that when the Vice President was education chief, she ordered him to give cash to school superintendents through their bank accounts.

The prosecution initially requested eight trial dates to present its bribery case, and listed four potential witnesses. They include those who allegedly received or were offered bribe money from Duterte’s office in DepEd, namely former DepEd undersecretary Gloria Jumamil-Mercado, and former bids and awards committee chair Resty Osias.
Malacañang previously sounded the alarm over the prosecution panel’s possible move to abandon the bribery case against the second-in-command.

“If they withdraw the bribery case against the Vice President, wouldn’t Filipinos who want to know the whole truth be shortchanged or be disadvantaged?” Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro had been quoted as saying. – Rappler.com

articles.title: [Vantage Point] The Senate’s Villar problem
articles.summary: Putting former DPWH secretary Mark Villar in charge of the oversight desk looks less like legislative stewardship and more like institutional conflict of interest

blocks.text: Putting former DPWH secretary Mark Villar in charge of the oversight desk looks less like legislative stewardship and more like institutional conflict of interest

items: Senator Mark Villar's transition from the minority to the majority in the Senate raises concerns about institutional independence amid ongoing scrutiny of his family's business dealings and flood-control scandals.

Villar's appointment as chair of the Senate committee on public works, overseeing projects linked to his previous role as secretary of the Department of Public Works and Highways, presents a potential conflict of interest.

The timing of Villar's political maneuvering coincides with legal investigations into his family's business practices, prompting questions about the Senate's commitment to credible oversight and accountability.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

As flood-control scandals raise uncomfortable questions about billions in infrastructure spending and his family’s corporate empire faces regulatory and legal scrutiny, Senator Mark Villar’s sudden leap to the majority—and into the public works committee chairmanship—puts a big question mark on the Senate’s institutional independence.
There are moments when the Senate seems bent on discovering just how far it can stretch the public’s capacity for disbelief.

While the floor was consumed by Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment proceedings, Senator Mark Villar executed a quiet migration from the minority to the majority. He did not arrive empty-handed. Without a peep of floor resistance, he walked away with two key levers of institutional influence: a seat on the Commission on Appointments and the chairmanship of the Senate committee on public works.

Meanwhile, across the aisle, his sister Camille stayed behind in the minority. It is the classic maneuver Filipinos know by instinct—namamangka sa dalawang ilog (playing both sides). Navigating both rivers at once guarantees that whatever current sweeps the chamber, the Villar family remains anchored on both banks.

blocks.caption: Mark Villar joins Senate majority | The wRap

blocks.text: They alone can speak to whether the split was coordinated, but in the transactional arithmetic of Philippine politics, having a foot in every camp is a survival strategy for any dynasty facing institutional heat. (READ: SEC chief Francis Lim to Villars: No family is too powerful to sue)
What makes this trade-off impossible to ignore is what Villar was handed: the legislative gavel over the very department he ran. (READ: DPWH post: Can Mark Villar rise above business interests?)

From 2016 to 2021, Mark Villar served as secretary of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) under Rodrigo Duterte. Those years sit squarely inside the timeline under review in the flood-control scandal, where billions of pesos in public funds yielded little more than submerged communities and unbuilt defenses. (READ: What’s a flood control project, anyway?)

When he was summoned to answer for projects greenlit under his watch, Villar denied improperly favoring family-linked contractors. Facing questions is not a finding of guilt. But it strains credibility to ask the public to trust that a Senate committee chair will fearlessly investigate his own administrative legacy. (READ: Firm owned by Senator Mark Villar’s uncle bagged P390M in flood control projects)
A committee chairmanship is not decorative. It sets the agenda, marshals witnesses, decides which scandals get dragged into daylight, and determines which files gather dust in an archive.

Even if Villar cannot award contracts from the rostrum, he holds the power to shape the inquiry. At an hour when taxpayers are demanding cold accounting for catastrophic flood projects, putting the former secretary in charge of the oversight desk looks less like legislative stewardship and more like institutional conflict of interest.

The legal entanglements do not end at the DPWH. Just this past September, the Ombudsman opened preliminary investigations into graft and administrative complaints against Villar family members, local water officials, and executives of PrimeWater over joint-venture agreements alleged to be disadvantageous to the public. Both Mark and Camille were named.

The family denies wrongdoing and insists it will defend itself through legal channels, but the fact remains: those agreements intersect directly with the years Mark sat in the Cabinet and held a seat on the Local Water Utilities Administration board.

Then came the afternoon’s corporate timing. Within an hour on Thursday, October 8, three Villar-controlled flagships—Vista Land & Lifescapes, Vistamalls, and VistaREIT—abruptly filed notices that their boards had cleared their long-overdue 2025 audited financial statements.

blocks.caption: Mark Villar switches camps. Minutes later, family’s troubled firms make their move.

blocks.text: These filings come after severe reporting delays led to trading suspensions across six Villar-linked firms. Board approval is not the same as audited accounts hitting the public tape, nor does it resolve overdue quarterly obligations.

Timing alone does not constitute evidence of backroom coordination, yet the optics are jarring: at the precise moment political power consolidated in the Senate, the family’s embattled business empire fired off a signal of operational survival.

This saga started in May 2025 when Vantage Point exposed the staggering arithmetic behind Villar Land—a P1.33-trillion property revaluation and an asserted profit of nearly a trillion pesos that quickly evaporated.

The subsequent reversal revealed the chasm between paper accounting and hard reality. Regulators soon disciplined the appraisal firm and launched complaints citing misleading disclosures, alleged market manipulation, and insider trading. The family denies wrongdoing, and due process must run its course, while AllDay and AllHome shutter retail outlets and Vista Land races to refinance debt.

This underscores the danger of letting private commercial distress collide with legislative oversight. Did Senate leaders ask a single hard question before handing him the committee? Did they demand recusal commitments for projects tied to his tenure or family enterprises? Who monitors the overseer?

Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri dismissed concerns by stating Villar’s party shift was unrelated to the impeachment fights. That may answer one concern, but it does nothing to clear the fog surrounding the public works gavel. When essential committees are handed out as political accommodations, legislative credibility disappears.

Filipinos have already paid the bill for suspect infrastructure, delayed dikes, and broken water projects. They should not also have to wonder if the Senate is running oversight with an eye toward preserving alliances. Like any citizen, Mark Villar is entitled to due process. But due process does not guarantee anyone the right to police their own past. The question is not whether he has the freedom to sit with the majority; he does. The real question is why the Senate decided to sacrifice the integrity of its own oversight just to give him a seat at the head of the table. – Rappler.com

articles.title: As freezing winter approaches, Kyiv residents look for shelter elsewhere
articles.summary: A renewed Russian campaign of strikes on power and energy infrastructure has made some contemplate leaving Ukraine's capital.

blocks.text: Watch: Olena explains what she cannot live near in order to stay safe
ByPaul Adams
Diplomatic correspondent, in Kyiv

As Russia's attacks on Ukraine's cities intensify and autumn's cooler temperatures hint at another tough winter to come, Ukrainians are wrestling with how to meet the twin challenges ahead: Russian drone and missile strikes and the biting cold.
"It was a very difficult winter last year in Kyiv," says mother of two Mariia Shostak, who is now packing her bags and leaving her small flat.
With prolonged periods of sub-zero temperatures and frequent power cuts brought about by Russia's attack on the country's power grid, last winter was one of the hardest so far.
"There were some days and weeks that were unbearable. I started thinking I'm not going through another winter like this."
Mariia is not even waiting for winter. Russia's latest assaults on the capital have forced her hand.
"Everything changed in late August and the beginning of September, when Kyiv started being attacked around the clock," she said.
"Earlier, the drones and missiles were intercepted somewhere on the outskirts. Now it was happening in the centre, right above our heads."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Wreckage from Russian drones can be found on the streets of the capital

blocks.text: Wreckage from Russian drones can be found on the streets of the capital

After weeks of escalating Russian attacks, which by the end of September had included petrol stations, power plants and key bridges over the Dnipro river, Kyiv mayor Vitaly Klitschko said the city was facing a "very dramatic situation".
The attacks, he said, were "tearing Kyiv apart".
Mariia's children, four-year-old Artur and Kira, who's two, were both born after Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

Unwilling to subject them to another miserable, dangerous winter, she's taking them abroad. They plan to spend the winter in Hurghada, on Egypt's Red Sea coast. It's cheaper than Europe, Mariia explains, and warmer too.
"I don't feel safe in Ukraine in any way," she says.
Polls show that many Ukrainians are feeling the same way, even if not everyone has yet made such a radical decision.

A September survey by the Gradus research company found that 40% of Ukrainians were considering relocating if living conditions continued to deteriorate; 35% said they would not move elsewhere, while 25% were undecided.

"People are thinking about a combination of stress factors," Evgeniya Blyznyuk, Gradus's founder and CEO, told us. "Not just about electricity and blackouts like last winter. Russians are targeting big logistics centres, which means that the population is worrying about products, about food during the winter."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Iryna's young daughter Polina is struggling to cope and suffers from anxiety

blocks.text: Iryna's young daughter Polina is struggling to cope and suffers from anxiety
Russia's recent attacks on Kyiv's bridges, petrol stations and schools have increased the sense of danger and foreboding.
For families with young children, the situation feels especially urgent.
Last winter, Iryna, who asked us not to use her surname, says her three-year-old daughter Polina found it hard to cope.
"Sometimes we didn't have heating for weeks and the temperature inside the apartment was zero or five degrees," she tells us. "So being here with a little child that is sick all the time was not OK."
The family's recent experiences have only compounded Polina's difficulties.
"We had two missile attacks this year," Iryna says.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Iryna and Polina's home is in this apartment block on the edge of the capital

blocks.text: Image source, Supplied
Iryna and Polina's home is in this apartment block on the edge of the capital

The first explosion, in early June, blew out several windows in the family's home on the north-western edge of Kyiv. A month later, after some of the damage had been repaired, a second blast, close to the foot of their 10-storey apartment block, propelled a wave of earth into the flat, forcing the family to move into temporary accommodation.
Polina's health has deteriorated. She suffers from extreme anxiety, which has brought on bouts of incontinence, vomiting and uncontrollable shaking.
"Now we have this neurological problem with her so that's the reason we're thinking about leaving," Iryna says. "There are new symptoms after each shelling."
Iryna, whose husband is in the army, has not yet decided where to go. Her work with an international NGO may allow her to work remotely from Poland.
"Our president says that it is better to leave Kyiv because this is target number one," she says.
For other Kyiv residents, the solution lies closer to home: in the vast open spaces of Ukraine's countryside.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Olena Konoplia says she is already sleeping better since her move to a more remote location

blocks.text: Olena Konoplia says she is already sleeping better since her move to a more remote location
Olena Konoplia tells us she spent weeks looking for a suitable location before settling on a cottage in a rural community two hours outside the capital.
"I decided the better option will be a little village without any factories, any [warehouses] and any railway stations," Olena explains.
"Everything that can be a Russian target."
On the day we visited, Olena was busy ferrying supplies to the house and supervising the installation of a new door.
In keeping with Ukrainian tradition, a priest has already been around to bless her new home.

The cottage has gas-powered convection heaters, but in an adjacent barn a stack of firewood will help to keep Olena warm in the event of power cuts. She has already installed high-speed internet, necessary for her work at a Kyiv-based charitable foundation.
At a time when air raid sirens sound constantly in Kyiv and explosions can be heard almost every day, the peace and quiet of the village is what Olena says she needs most.
"After several nights here, when I can sleep, just sleep, without any explosions, without any sirens, I feel better," she says. "I can work, write my articles, I feel good."
Olena's elderly mother will soon be joining her.
"She lives in a pretty dangerous district in Kyiv and it's harmful for her health," she explains.
Of course, not everyone can afford a cottage in the countryside or a months-long trip abroad.
Most Kyiv residents will do what they can to survive another tough winter in the capital, just as they have before.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Supermarkets in Kyiv have been experiencing shortages of goods at times

blocks.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images
Supermarkets in Kyiv have been experiencing shortages of goods at times

The authorities are taking steps to prepare. Some of Kyiv's most vulnerable citizens – the elderly and women with young children – are being offered places in converted sanatoriums and rehabilitation centres in the city's forested outskirts.
Meanwhile, a network of around 15 small-scale power plants has been constructed around the city over the past 18 months in an effort to shore up Kyiv's battered power grid.

The plants, constructed in fortified bunkers and protected from drone attack by huge steel cages, are each capable of providing electricity and heat to several hundred of the city's high-rise apartment blocks.
But with energy companies already talking about scheduled power cuts and supermarkets experiencing periodic shortages of some goods, the pressures to leave are growing.

Evgeniya Blyznyuk says she does not expect to see a mass exodus from the capital and says most people have yet to make up their minds, reluctant to jeopardise their jobs or take children out of school.
"They will postpone it until conditions become really unliveable," she says.

articles.title: Marcos to attend Singapore F1 Grand Prix 2026
articles.summary: Malacañang on Friday confirmed that President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. will attend the Formula 1 race in Singapore, scheduled to start on October 9, 2026.

blocks.text: PALACE SAYS
Published October 9, 2026 12:45pm
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. will attend the Formula 1 race in Singapore, scheduled to start on October 9, 2026.

“Dadalo po siya dahil ang sabi ng Pangulo ang mga transaction mas magandang nagkakaroon ng face-to-face meetings katulad ng ganitong event,” Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said during a press briefing in Singapore on Friday.
(He will attend because, as the President said, transactions and discussions are better conducted through face-to-face meetings at events like this.)
“Naipahayag niya rin na minsan sa ganitong event niya nakita si Lee Kuan Yew at ilang mga negosyante na nakikita ang body language ng bawat isa,” she added.
(He also shared that it was at a similar event where he met Lee Kuan Yew and several business leaders, emphasizing the value of observing one another's body language.)
The Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix events start Friday while the main race is scheduled on October 11.
Marcos has previously stated that attending the event presents partnership opportunities for the Philippines.
According to Ambassador Medardo Macaraig, Marcos was invited by Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, and noted that the President will not need to pay for a ticket.
Castro previously said that Marcos’ attendance at the race is bound to draw attention.
“Hindi maiiwasan na may pipintas, at may negatibo pero hindi nawawala kahit isang segundo ang pagiging Pangulo ni Pangulong Marcos,” Castro said.
(Criticism and negative comments are inevitable, but President Marcos does not stop being President even for a single second.)
Marcos has already attended at least two other Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix events during his presidency. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Cars torched and shops looted as anti-migrant violence erupts in South Africa
articles.summary: South Africa has experienced recurrent outbreaks of violence, often targeting migrants from neighbouring countries.

blocks.text: Thursday's demonstration turned violent following allegations that a foreign national had assaulted one of the protesters in Durban.
Three foreign nationals were arrested in connection with the alleged assault, police said.
In Durban, in the eastern province of KwaZulu-Natal, protesters gathered outside a government refugee reception centre demanding that it stop accepting asylum applications.
Police fired rubber bullets to disperse crowds as businesses in the city centre shut their doors.
"There were clashes between foreign nationals in the area and South African nationals," senior local police officer Xolani Fihla told state broadcaster SABC.
"At the present moment, I can confirm that no injuries have been reported," he added.
Police said 14 vehicles were torched in Durban and 10 in Soweto, where gunshots were also reported during confrontations between residents and foreign shopkeepers.
Acting national police commissioner Lt Gen Puleng Dimpane condemned the destruction of property.
In Orlando West, a neighbourhood of Soweto, residents had initially gathered to demand the closure of small convenience stores, known locally as spaza shops, operated by foreign nationals.
Protesters forced foreign traders out of some areas, while shops were attacked and a building was set on fire, local media reported.
Police said reinforcements had been deployed to prevent further violence.
The authorities have promised to pursue those responsible for the destruction.

The latest unrest follows a July ruling by South Africa's Constitutional Court, the country's highest court, which struck down restrictions preventing some people from seeking asylum because of how they entered the country or missed immigration deadlines.
The judgment means asylum seekers must be allowed to submit applications, even if they entered South Africa without the required documents.
It has prompted hundreds of people to gather at refugee reception centres, fuelling anger among anti-immigration campaigners who fear the decision will encourage undocumented migration.

Government spokesman William Baloyi told Reuters news agency that people had deliberately spread false claims about the judgment, creating the impression that undocumented migrants would automatically be granted legal status.
Baloyi insisted that the ruling does not automatically give migrants refugee status or the right to remain permanently in South Africa.
Officials say applications will still be assessed individually and applicants will remain subject to immigration checks.
Earlier this year, anti-immigration groups staged weeks of demonstrations demanding that undocumented foreign nationals leave the country by 30 June.
The protests forced tens of thousands of migrants to flee, with some returning home through repatriation programmes organised by their governments.
South Africa has struggled with xenophobic attacks for nearly two decades. In 2008, more than 60 people were killed and tens of thousands displaced during widespread attacks on foreign nationals.
The latest unrest comes against a backdrop of widespread poverty, deep inequality and unemployment affecting roughly a third of the workforce.
Migrants are frequently accused of taking jobs, contributing to crime and placing pressure on public services, although researchers say such sweeping claims are not supported by evidence.
Despite its economic difficulties, South Africa remains one of the continent's main destinations for migrants seeking employment, safety and better opportunities.

articles.title: PCG: China Coast Guard delays PH Navy personnel's medical evacuation from Ayungin Shoal
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said the China Coast Guard (CCG) obstructed and delayed the emergency medical evacuation of a Philippine Navy personnel from Ayungin Shoal for nearly 10 hours on…

blocks.text: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said the China Coast Guard (CCG) obstructed and delayed the emergency medical evacuation of a Philippine Navy personnel from Ayungin Shoal for nearly 10 hours on Thursday.
In a statement, PCG spokesperson Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said BRP Cabra was deployed from Lawak Island to evacuate the ailing personnel stationed aboard BRP Sierra Madre.

“On 08 October 2026, the PCG completed the emergency MEDEVAC of a Philippine Navy personnel stationed aboard BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal. CCG vessels obstructed and delayed the mission for nearly ten hours,” he said.
In a separate statement, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) said the personnel required immediate medical attention due to a pre-existing medical condition.
AFP’s Western Command coordinated with the PCG and other concerned agencies to facilitate his safe evacuation and transfer to an appropriate medical facility.

“The AFP remains focused on the health, safety, and welfare of its personnel. Every necessary measure is being taken to ensure that the patient receives the medical attention and care he needs at the soonest possible time,” the military said.
GMA News Online has sought comment from the Chinese Embassy in Manila but it has yet to respond as of posting time.
Water cannon

Around 7:30 a.m., Tarriela said BRP Cabra reached a position about nine nautical miles north of Ayungin Shoal when CCG vessel 5306, which had been shadowing the Philippine vessel, activated its water cannon.
The Chinese vessel continued using its water cannon as it approached BRP Cabra, moving from about 1.3 nautical miles away to roughly 400 yards, according to Tarriela.
While BRP Cabra was not hit by the water cannon, Tarriela said the Philippine vessel moved away from the shoal to ensure the safety of its vessel and crew.
The PCG initially proposed a rendezvous point about 2.5 nautical miles northeast of BRP Sierra Madre, but the CCG did not allow the arrangement, according to Tarriela.
“BRP Cabra was held about 13 nautical miles north of the shoal for several hours,” Tarriela said.
At 12:52 p.m., CCG vessel 5306 again radio-challenged BRP Cabra and insisted on a different rendezvous point farther from BRP Sierra Madre.
The PCG said it adjusted its operations to prioritize the patient's welfare.
At 1:46 p.m., BRP Cabra launched a rigid-hull inflatable boat (RHIB) carrying PCG personnel, a maritime security team member, and Coast Guard medical personnel.
Within a minute, the CCG deployed its own RHIB that shadowed the Philippine boat throughout its 9.2-nautical-mile transit to the rendezvous point.
BRP Sierra Madre also launched two rubber boats toward the meeting point, one of which carried the patient, Tarriela said.
Around 3:15 p.m., the patient and his companion were safely transferred to the PCG RHIB.
During the return trip, CCG vessel 21585 shadowed the Philippine boat at about 500 yards, while CCG vessel 5306 remained about 600 yards off its port quarter.
The PCG RHIB reached BRP Cabra shortly before 5 p.m. without further incident.
A PCG medical officer immediately examined the patient, checked his vital signs, and administered intravenous fluids.
The patient is now stable and being transported to the nearest suitable port for further treatment, according to Tarriela.
Monitored during the operation were CCG vessels 5306, 5009, and 21585, Chinese maritime militia vessel Qiongsanshayu 00119, and People's Liberation Army Navy warship 628.

The PCG said a transfer of this kind would normally take only a few hours but was prolonged by the water cannon incident, the disagreement over the rendezvous point, and the continued shadowing of Philippine vessels.

PCG Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan said, "When a life is at stake, there should be no water cannon, no obstruction, and no delay. Saving a sick or injured person at sea is a basic obligation that every coast guard in the world is expected to uphold.

“We call on the China Coast Guard to value and respect humanitarian missions moving forward, and to act in a manner consistent with international law and the professional standards expected of any coast guard.)
BRP Sierra Madre
The BRP Sierra Madre has been grounded at Ayungin Shoal since 1999 and serves as an outpost for Philippine troops in the disputed waters.
The Ayungin Shoal — called Ren’ai Reef by China — is a submerged reef in the Spratly Islands, which is a group of more than 100 islands and reefs in the South China Sea.
It is located 105 nautical miles west of Palawan and is within the country’s 200-mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and is part of its continental shelf.

Tensions continue as Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea, a conduit for more than $3 trillion of annual shipborne commerce, including parts claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.
Parts of the South China Sea that fall within Philippine territory have been renamed by the government as West Philippine Sea to reinforce the country’s claim.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago, including the Luzon Sea and the waters around, within, and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines over China's claims in the South China Sea, saying that it had "no legal basis."
China has refused to recognize the decision. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: BIR witness: No deadline to file fraud case vs. taxpayer, just the assessment
articles.summary: The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) does not have deadline to discover fraud and file the consequent charge for it, but has 10 years from the date of discovery to assess the case, a witness from the…

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 12:42pm

The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) does not have deadline to discover fraud and file the consequent charge for it, but has 10 years from the date of discovery to assess the case, a witness from the tax agency said Friday.

On Day 37 of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, defense counsel Kristine Ferrer asked lawyer Anne Loraine Garcia-Marquez, chief of staff of the BIR Office of the Commissioner, about the prescriptive period when the bureau can audit the accounts of someone suspected of fraud.
"Assuming the fraud is discovered in 2026, the farthest year that the BIR can assess is 2016?" Ferrer asked in her cross-examination.

House private prosecutor Erwin Matib objected to the question, calling the question misleading. Impeachment Presiding Officer Francis "Chiz" Escudero also took issue with the question's wording, sustaining Matib's objection.

"My understanding is 10 years from the… the prescriptive period is 10 years from the date of discovery, not that you can only look back for only 10 years from the time that you discovered it. That's different," Escudero said.
Ferrer rephrased the question, asking: "Assuming fraud is discovered in 2016… the latest that you can assess in the year 2026?"
However, Garcia-Marquez said that the 10 years prescriptive date is merely for the discovery of the fraud, not the taxable year that the fraud was allegedly committed.

"I will clarify again.… you discover the fraud in 2026, so you have 10 years from 2026 to assess or to conduct an audit in the particular taxable year," Garcia-Marquez said in a mix of English and Filipino.
Escudero then asked the witness if there was a prescriptive period for the BIR to make a discovery of fraud, to which Garcia-Marquez said that there was none.
"What about a taxable year, 1992? Hanggang ngayon ba, 'pag may nakita kayong fraud, you can still look into it and file a case in relation to it?" Escudero asked.
(What about a taxable year, 1992? Until now, if you see fraud, you can still look into it and file a case in relation to it?)
To which Garcia-Marquez responded: "Yes po, your honor."
Garcia-Marquez was called as a witness for the prosecution regarding Article 2 of the Duterte's impeachment case, accusing her of unexplained wealth. — VDV, GMA News

CAGAYAN DE ORO, Philippines – Lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio, husband of Vice President Sara Duterte, said he felt he was being targeted amid the impeachment proceedings against his wife, describing himself as “collateral damage” as the couple’s finances came under scrutiny.
Speaking at a 1Bukidnon4 Sara Duterte Movement event in Valencia City on Thursday, October 8, Carpio said he felt he was being treated unfairly.
“Medyo gidaogdaog man ta karon,” Carpio said in a video clip posted on local broadcaster RMN-Malaybalay’s Facebook page.
(I feel like I’m being persecuted a bit now.)

blocks.caption: LIST: Duterte-Carpio bank accounts, balances detailed in impeachment trial

blocks.text: “Tanan sa gobyerno gigamit,” he added, saying “Murag ako ang gi-impeach da,” Carpio said.
(Government resources were being used…. It’s as if I’m the one who was impeached.)
Carpio described himself as “collateral damage” and said he was praying that the situation would pass.

blocks.caption: Hontiveros: China state-owned businesses remitted funds to Sara Duterte-linked Cale88

blocks.text: His remarks came as the impeachment proceedings against Duterte brought the couple’s finances to public scrutiny as the trial entered its 36th day. The impeachment court continued tackling their taxes and documents from the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) on Friday, October 9.

Carpio and his wife’s lawyers had fought to keep the couple’s financial records out of public view, invoking confidentiality rules. Carpio had argued that he was a private citizen, and that his finances should remain private.
Carpio’s name has been repeatedly mentioned by the prosecution in its presentation of the unexplained wealth case against the Vice President.

Earlier this week, a witness from the Anti-Money Laundering Council told the court that, of the P4.4 billion in large and suspicious transactions that flowed through the couple’s bank accounts from 2007 to 2025, P749 million was attributed to Carpio alone.
The witness also said Carpio withdrew P41 million in cash through multiple over-the-counter transactions in a single day in 2024.
The findings are significant because Duterte declared minimal to zero cash on hand and in bank accounts in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs) over the years.
The AMLC also said Cale88, a food company Carpio founded, received P319 million in remittances from Chinese corporations.
The company’s corporate filings no longer list him in its general information sheet as of 2025, but the BIR said it has no record of him having sold the company.– Rappler.com

articles.title: ICE agent shoots man in New York City
articles.summary: The mayor of New York expressed outrage at the shooting which the Department of Homeland Security said happened during the arrest of a "criminal illegal alien".

blocks.text: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot a man in the Bronx in New York City on Thursday.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which runs the agency, confirmed an ICE officer "discharged his weapon" during "a targeted enforcement operation... to arrest a criminal illegal alien".
In a statement, it added the man was alive and at a local hospital.
New York mayor Zohran Mamdani said it was an "unconscionable and incredibly serious situation".
"Early reports indicate agents surrounded him and a five-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds. We believe the child was physically unharmed," he said.
The BBC has approached DHS for comment about Mamdani's remarks.
Late on Thursday evening, New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she had spoken to President Donald Trump about the shooting and had expressed "outrage on behalf of New Yorkers".
"I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public so we can establish the facts and get to the truth."
Trump has not yet commented publicly on the shooting.

The DHS said the man, who has not been named by officials, was from the Dominican Republic and had "a prior criminal conviction for grand larceny, and multiple prior arrests for assault, robbery, possession of drugs, and weapons possession".
He was arrested by police officers in New York in December 2023 and released "a few days later", according to the DHS statement.
It also claimed he was associated with the Trinitarios, described by the US justice department as a transnational criminal group.
